q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text: Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to a child over 6 months old for fever, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Give it every 6 to 8 hours, and check the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine is suitable for your child [3][6]. Know your child's weight before giving it [6]. Do not give ibuprofen if your child is dehydrated, has chickenpox, or has asthma unless a doctor recommends it [2]. Keep breastfeeding as normal and offer plenty of fluids [3]. q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the common causes [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, so the priority is to keep fluids going in [3].

When your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give oral rehydration solution — 2 to 5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, according to the SEUP [5]. Watch how well they take it; if they keep it down, you can slowly give it more often [5]. Don't use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks [5]. Oral rehydration fluids from the pharmacy are the most helpful for mild dehydration, and sports drinks without caffeine can help a little, though they don't replace lost minerals, the CDC says [2].

If your child is very drowsy, vomits many times, or won't take any fluids, see your paediatrician [3]. If you think they are severely dehydrated, call your doctor [2].

A cough that is worse at night is common in children with asthma, and it can also be the main sign of it [6]. Asthma symptoms usually come and go and are often worse at night and early in the morning [4].

If your child has asthma, keep using their inhaler as usual and check that they are using it correctly [4]. If they do not have a diagnosis yet, note when the cough happens — at night, early morning, or after exercise, cold air or contact with pets, dust or pollen [4].

See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, if treatment is not helping, if they need their inhaler more often, or if symptoms are waking them at night [4]. q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. If the cough comes in bouts that are worse at night, or your son makes a "whoop" sound gasping between coughs, that points to whooping cough: after about a week of cold-like symptoms, the cough comes in bouts lasting a few minutes, often with a whoop, thick mucus that can make him vomit, or a red face [4]. The cough can then last several weeks or months [4].

If you think it may be whooping cough, ask your doctor to see him — they may give medicine to shorten the illness, and it is worth checking sooner if he is getting worse or not getting better [3].

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, and most children recover quickly [3][6]. The usual symptoms after a knock to the head are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness [1].

For the next 24 hours, keep an eye on him for symptoms that could mean it is getting worse [3]. Let him rest, physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the knock was — no sport and no screens during that time, then a gradual return to normal activity [4]. He can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. He can eat normally, as his appetite dictates [6]. If he has a headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol at the dose your doctor indicates [6].

Get urgent medical help if he has been knocked out and has not woken up, cannot stay awake, has a seizure, has vision or hearing problems, has clear fluid or blood coming from his ears or nose, has bruising behind his ears, has new numbness or weakness, has trouble walking, balancing, understanding or speaking, or if his behaviour has changed [2]. Also go if the headache is severe or getting worse and does not ease with the usual medicine, if he vomits repeatedly, if he is confused or disoriented, or if there is blood or clear fluid from his nose or ears [4].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text: Start with single vegetables and fruits: mashed or soft, cooked sticks of parsnip, broccoli, potato, yam, sweet potato, carrot, apple or pear, according to the NHS [1]. Include vegetables that are not sweet, such as broccoli, cauliflower and spinach, so your baby gets used to a range of flavours [1]. Make sure any cooked food has cooled right down before offering it [1]. Foods containing allergens, such as peanuts, hens' eggs, gluten and fish, can be introduced from around 6 months, one at a time and in small amounts so you can spot any reaction [1]. Full-fat dairy products like pasteurised cheese and plain yoghurt can be given from around 6 months; choose ones with no added sugar [1]. Babies do not need salt or sugar added to their food or cooking water [1]. At first, how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to eating — they still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [2].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text: For a 9-month-old, breast milk or infant formula should still be the main drink during the first year, according to the NHS [3]. Offer sips of water with meals, ideally from an open cup or a free-flow cup without a valve — this helps your baby learn to sip and is better for their teeth [3]. There is no set amount given; let your baby take small sips alongside food and keep milk feeds as usual. Around this age, formula-fed babies may have about 3 milk feeds a day and drink roughly 400 ml of formula daily [5]. If they are having less than 500 ml of formula a day, they should take vitamin A, C and D supplements [5].

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: It is common for babies to prefer fruit, and you can keep offering vegetables alongside it. From about 7 months, aim for 3 meals a day plus their usual milk feeds, and gradually increase the amount and variety of food offered [2]. Include iron-rich foods such as meat, fish, fortified breakfast cereals, dark green vegetables, beans and lentils, and offer fruit and vegetables including bitter ones like broccoli, cauliflower, spinach and cabbage [2]. Finger foods at each meal help babies feed themselves and learn to chew [2]. Babies do not need salt or sugar added to their food or cooking water [2]. Vegetables help improve iron intake, so they are worth persisting with even if your baby refuses them at first [5].

At 13 months, formula is no longer needed: cows' milk can be introduced as a main drink from 12 months, and formula milks are not needed once your baby is 12 months old [2]. q: how often should a newborn poop
text: How often a newborn poops varies from baby to baby — the rhythm and consistency of stools differ from one person to another, and it is not essential that a baby has a bowel movement every day, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more is the consistency: constipation is when stools become too hard, with discomfort or incomplete emptying, and it may come with fewer bowel movements [6]. In a baby under 6 months, keep feeding as usual with breast milk or formula [3]. Do not give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [3]. See your doctor if there is blood in the stool, a lot of tummy pain, or the baby vomits many times and cannot keep down solids or liquids [3].

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on mainly when he lies down can be a sign of asthma, which often causes coughing at night or early in the morning [3]. Other common causes of cough include a cold or flu, heartburn (acid reflux), allergies, or mucus dripping down the throat from the back of the nose [2].

Offer water to drink, or add moisture to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer, which can help ease the cough [1]. Do not give cough medicine to a child under four; for children over four, use caution and read labels carefully [1].

See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if symptoms are waking him up at night [5]. Get medical help right away for severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or turning very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [3].

On steam, guidelines differ. The CDC suggests sitting with a young child in a bathroom with steam from a running shower to ease a cough. The NHS advises against it: with croup, do not put your child in a steamy room or get them to inhale steam, and do not let children breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, because of the risk of scalding.

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text:
Needing your reliever inhaler more often is a sign the asthma is not as well controlled as it should be, and it is a reason to see your doctor [2]. Asthma is treated with inhalers that open the airways and reduce inflammation, and most people do well when the right treatment is used correctly [1][3].

Keep using the reliever inhaler when your son has symptoms, and make sure it is used with a spacer if he has one — a spacer helps the medicine reach the lungs [1]. Do not change or add any other medicine on your own; the dose and type of inhaler are decided by his doctor [1][3].

See your doctor because he is needing his inhaler more often, and also if symptoms are waking him at night or stopping him doing his usual activities [2]. If he has an asthma attack — severe breathing difficulty — sit him up straight, stay calm, and use the reliever inhaler as his action plan says [4].

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be croup: an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe that causes noisy, high-pitched breathing, a dry barking cough and a hoarse voice, and it often starts like a cold [3]. Most viral croup is mild and can be treated at home, and symptoms usually get worse at night and last three to five days [3].

Keep her calm and comfortable, and let her rest; offer fluids often in small amounts. Croup is most common between six months and three years, and more frequent in autumn and winter [3].

If you are worried about your child's breathing, call your doctor straight away, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Signs that breathing is getting harder include breathing fast, the ribs pulling in, the chest sinking in, or tiring when walking or running [1].

q: my baby had a seizure last year and has a fever today
text:
A fever is very common in young children and usually settles within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [1]. A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature; it can seem frightening, but it is unlikely to harm your child or cause long-term effects [3].

If your child has another seizure: do not move them or try to hold them in place, do not put anything in their mouth, and do not try to lower their temperature by undressing them or sponging them with cold water [5]. Time the seizure — they usually last 2 to 3 minutes, and it is rare for them to last more than 10 minutes [2].

Get medical help if your child has a seizure, according to the NHS [3]. Call your local emergency number or go to the emergency department if a seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, they have trouble breathing, the stiffness and twitching are on only one side, they are more sleepy than usual for more than 1 hour afterwards, or they have more than one seizure within 24 hours [2].

q: my 4 year old had a seizure when he was a baby, does that change anything now
text:
A seizure with a fever (a febrile seizure) is not usually serious and is unlikely to harm your child or cause long-term effects, according to the NHS [2]. Having had one does not mean your child has epilepsy — they are not the same thing, though children who have had a febrile seizure have a slightly increased chance of epilepsy later in life, and this is rare [3].

If your child ever has another seizure, keep them safe while you wait for medical help: check the time it starts and ends, protect their head with your hands or something soft, and move dangerous objects away [4]. q: my daughter is 13 and started her period but has very heavy bleeding
text:
Heavy periods are common, and they can be normal — especially when periods first start [3]. They are worth looking at when they affect daily life, and treatment can help [2].

Signs that bleeding is heavy: needing to change a pad or tampon every 1 to 2 hours, using two products together, periods lasting more than 7 days, clots bigger than about 2.5 cm, bleeding through to clothes or bedding, or feeling tired or short of breath [2].

Heavy menstrual bleeding can lead to anaemia, so it should be treated [4][5]. Eating iron-rich foods — lean red meat, fish, poultry, lentils and beans, fortified cereals, dark green leafy vegetables — and foods rich in vitamin C helps the body absorb iron [6].

See your doctor if the heavy periods are affecting her life, have gone on for some time, come with severe pain, or if she bleeds between periods [3].

q: my 15 year old has acne that is getting worse
text:
Acne is a common skin condition that causes spots ranging from mild to severe, and it usually affects the face, chest and back [5]. It can also affect your child's mental health, causing anxiety, depression and low self-esteem [5].

To help at home, have them wash their skin twice a day with a gentle cleanser, remove make-up at the end of the day, and use non-comedogenic skincare and make-up products that will not clog pores [1]. They can try treatments you put on the skin such as salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide, and a pharmacist can advise on these [1]. Do not pick or squeeze spots, as this can cause scars, and do not scrub the skin, as this can irritate it and make acne worse [1].

See a doctor if they have tried treating it themselves but it is not getting better, if there are lots of spots or the spots are deep, painful or causing scars, if there are signs of a skin infection such as hot, swollen and red skin, or if it is affecting their mental health [3]. A doctor can offer prescription treatments that are stronger than what you can buy, or refer them to a skin specialist [3].

q: my child says his heart is beating really fast after an energy drink
text:
A fast, noticeable heartbeat is called a palpitation: it can feel like racing, pounding or fluttering, and it can last seconds, minutes or longer, according to the NHS [1]. Palpitations are common and not usually a sign of anything serious, and caffeine is one of the common causes [2].

Avoiding the things that can trigger palpitations — caffeine, alcohol, smoking and stress — can help when they are not caused by a health condition [5]. Energy drinks contain caffeine, so keeping him off them is the practical step.

See a doctor if the palpitations keep coming back or are happening more often, if they last longer than a few minutes, or if he has a heart condition or a family history of heart problems [2]. Get help straight away if they do not go away, or if he also has chest pain, shortness of breath, or feels faint or faints [2].

q: my toddler has a swollen eyelid after waking up
text: A swollen eyelid on waking can be an early sign of roseola, a very common infection in babies and toddlers that usually causes a high temperature and a rash [3]. At first they may have a sudden high temperature, cold-like symptoms such as a sore throat, runny nose and cough, loss of appetite, and swollen eyelids and swollen glands in the neck [3]. These symptoms last 3 to 5 days, before a rash appears [3]. The rash is made up of pinkish-red spots, patches or bumps, starts on the chest, tummy and back before spreading to the face, neck and arms, and normally fades within 2 days [3]. You can normally look after your child at home and they should recover within a week [3].

text:

What to do now: check the temperature with a thermometer, under the arm is fine [4]. If the child is uncomfortable with a fever above 38ºC (100.4 °F), give the antipyretic your paediatrician usually recommends [5]; the dose depends on the child's age and weight, so follow what your doctor or the leaflet gives. Do not give aspirin to a child under 16 [1].

text:
A child who says he feels he cannot catch his breath needs to be checked, even when the monitor reads 99. Difficulty breathing is one of the signs to watch for at home, according to the SEUP: ribs pulling in or the chest sinking, breathing fast, tiring when walking or running, or chest pain when breathing [2]. The monitor reading alone does not rule this out. The SEUP lists difficulty breathing as a reason to seek urgent care, along with a child who is limp, sleepy or very irritable [2]. The WHO also counts fast breathing or pulling in below the ribs as signs of a chest infection in a child with a cough [6].

If he is struggling to speak, breathing fast, or his chest is sinking in, get him seen now.

text:
Flushed cheeks can be a sign of a high temperature in a baby, so it is worth checking with a thermometer [2]. A normal temperature in babies is about 36.4C (97.5 °F), and a high temperature is usually considered to be 38C (100.4 °F) or above [2]. q: my daughter has a cough after visiting someone who had COVID
text:
A cough after being near someone with COVID can be a common cold or another respiratory virus; most cold symptoms get better on their own with time, according to the CDC [3]. RSV, for example, usually causes a mild, cold-like illness with coughing, and symptoms often begin 2 to 8 days after exposure [5].

There is no antiviral that works against the ordinary respiratory viruses that cause cold symptoms [3]. Keep her comfortable and offer fluids; if she is at higher risk of severe illness from COVID-19 or flu, contact your healthcare provider right away, even if her illness is mild, because early antiviral treatment works best when started soon after symptoms begin [2].

Seek medical care if she has trouble breathing or fast breathing, dehydration, a fever lasting longer than 4 days, or symptoms that last more than 10 days without getting better or that improve then worsen [2].

q: my son had croup last winter and now has a barking cough again
text:
A barking cough with a hoarse voice and noisy breathing is how croup shows up, and it is usually caused by a virus [1]. Most cases are mild and can be treated at home, and symptoms are often worse at night [1]. They usually settle in a few days, though they can last up to a week [4].

Offer fluids if there is a fever and give the usual fever medicine [4]. Water can help ease the cough, whether your child drinks it or you add it to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer [6]. Do not give cough medicine to a child under four [6].

Watch your child's breathing and their colour and general condition, because the swelling can make it harder to get air in [4]. If you are worried about your child's breathing, call your doctor right away [1].

On steam, guidelines differ. The CDC suggests sitting with a young child in a bathroom with steam from a running shower to ease a cough. The NHS advises against it: with croup, do not put your child in a steamy room or get them to inhale steam, and do not let children breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, because of the risk of scalding.

q: my son has a rash after swimming in a lake
text:
A rash that comes up after swimming in a lake is often hives — raised, itchy bumps or patches that can appear anywhere on the body and look pink or red on white skin, though they can be harder to see on brown or black skin [1]. In childhood, most hives are caused by an infection, and an allergic cause is less common [4].

What you can do at home: avoid rubbing the skin and avoid very hot baths or showers [5]. Do not put powders or creams on the skin, and do not give any syrup, without checking with your doctor first [5]. Your child can eat their usual food, without introducing anything new [5]. A pharmacist can advise about antihistamine treatment for hives, though this may not be suitable for young children [7].

Get help straight away if your child's lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell, they struggle to breathe or swallow, their skin, tongue or lips turn blue, grey or pale, or they become limp, floppy or not responding as usual — these can be signs of a serious allergic reaction [7].

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text:
The most common early symptoms of malaria are fever, headache and chills, and they usually start within 10–15 days of being bitten by an infected mosquito [1][2]. Because these symptoms are not specific, getting tested early matters [2]. Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1].

If your child has fever, headache or chills after travelling to a malaria area, get them tested for malaria early — early treatment of mild malaria can stop it becoming severe [2].

Severe symptoms include extreme tiredness, impaired consciousness, multiple convulsions, difficulty breathing, dark or bloody urine, jaundice and abnormal bleeding; someone with these needs emergency care right away [2].

q: my child coughs mostly at night but is fine during the day
text:
A cough that is worse at night and fine during the day is a common pattern in asthma: a persistent cough, especially at night, is one of its usual symptoms, according to the WHO [3]. The NHS adds that asthma symptoms often come and go and may be worse at night and early in the morning [4].

Keep a note of when the cough happens and what seems to set it off — colds, cold air, dust, pollen, pets, smoke or exercise are all known triggers [5]. There is no need to give cough medicine: children under four should not have it at all, and for children over four you should use caution and read labels carefully [1]. Water can help ease a cough, whether they drink it or you add it to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer [1].

See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if symptoms are waking them at night or stopping them doing their usual activities [4].

On steam, guidelines differ. The CDC suggests sitting with a young child in a bathroom with steam from a running shower to ease a cough. The NHS advises against it: with croup, do not put your child in a steamy room or get them to inhale steam, and do not let children breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, because of the risk of scalding.

text: A dry cough is a common symptom of RSV and other respiratory viruses in babies, and most cold-like symptoms are not usually a sign of anything serious [3]. There is no specific treatment for RSV; it usually clears up on its own in 1 to 2 weeks [5]. q: my daughter has a wet cough but no fever
text:
A wet cough with no fever is most often part of a common cold, and fever itself is just the body's normal response to infections like coughs and colds [1]. There is no need to treat a fever that is not there, and no medicine is needed for the cough itself.

q: my daughter fainted for a few seconds at school and feels fine now
text:
A short faint like this is called a syncope: a sudden, brief loss of consciousness that happens when not enough blood or oxygen reaches the brain, according to the SEUP [2]. It often follows heat, pain, fear, nervousness, standing still for a long time, or getting up suddenly [2].

If she starts to feel unwell again, have her sit or lie down straight away, and breathe slowly and deeply [5]. If she faints, lay her down with her legs raised and her head to one side so she breathes better [5]. When the discomfort has passed, she can get up slowly — sit first, then stand after a few minutes [5]. After resting, children usually recover quickly, within a couple of minutes [5].

Get urgent help if she takes more than 3 to 5 minutes to come round, if the faint happened during exercise or while sitting, or if it came with palpitations, chest pain, jerking of the limbs or passing urine [6].

text:
Blurry vision after a hit to the face can be a sign of concussion, a temporary brain injury caused by a blow that makes the head and brain move quickly back and forth [6]. A concussion can happen even without passing out, and symptoms can take hours or days to appear [6].

Have your child checked by a doctor, and keep someone watching them for the next few days [6]. Rest is important to help the brain heal; in the beginning, limit physical activity and anything that needs a lot of concentration, like screens or studying, since these can bring symptoms back or make them worse [5]. Return to normal activities slowly, only when your doctor says it is okay [5].

Get help right away for neck pain, double vision, loss of consciousness, a seizure, repeated vomiting, or a headache that is severe or getting worse [4].

banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 911 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado)
text: El asma es una enfermedad en la que los bronquios se obstruyen y provocan tos, dificultad para respirar y silbidos en el pecho, según la SEUP [2]. text:
A temperature of 98.6 °F is normal, not a fever — a fever is usually 100.4 °F (38 °C (100.4 °F)) or higher, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Feeling hot to touch on the back or chest, sweaty or clammy, or having flushed cheeks can suggest a high temperature even when the reading looks normal [4].

Ear and forehead strip thermometers are less accurate in young children [5].

text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

For an older child, a rash that appears just as the fever drops is a recognised pattern. q: what are the side effects of chickenpox shot
text: Most side effects of the chickenpox vaccine are mild and do not last long, according to the NHS [2]. They can include swelling or pain where the injection was given, a high temperature, and a rash at the injection site or more widespread, usually within 1 month of vaccination [2]. A combined MMRV vaccine can also cause a raised, blotchy rash, feeling unwell and a high temperature about 6 to 10 days later, or a spotty rash like chickenpox about 3 to 4 weeks later; that spotty rash may contain infectious chickenpox virus and should be covered with clothes [5]. More serious side effects, such as a severe allergic reaction, are very rare, and the person who vaccinates your child is trained to treat them immediately [2][5]. The chickenpox vaccine is the best way to prevent chickenpox [3].

text: A blocked, noisy nose at night is common in babies, and illnesses can affect how your baby sleeps [6]. Ear infections are the most common reason parents bring a child to the doctor, and tugging at the ear and crying more than usual are two of the signs to look for, according to MedlinePlus [1]. q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard, dry poop that hurts to pass is common and usually not serious [3]. It means the stool has become too hard, sometimes with small tears around the anus that make it hurt more [4].

What helps: offer more liquids, preferably water, to soften the stool [1]. Add more fiber — whole grains and fiber-rich bread, fruits and vegetables — and don't replace fruit with juice, since juice has little fiber [1]. Keep a regular routine and don't let him hold in the urge to go [1]. Laxatives or enemas should only be given if a pediatrician recommends them [1].

It's not important that he poops every day — normal rhythm and consistency vary from person to person [1][3].

See a doctor if there is blood in the stool, severe belly pain, or he is very down and vomiting a lot and can't keep down solids or liquids [1].

q: my child keeps scratching red patches on his arms
text:
Itchy red patches on the arms are common in children and often fit atopic eczema, a long-lasting skin condition that cannot be cured but can be managed, according to the NHS [1]. Scratching itself can make skin red, swollen and itchier, MedlinePlus adds [2].

What helps: apply a moisturising treatment (emollient) at least twice a day, and keep going even when the skin improves [5]. Wash with an emollient instead of soap, avoid things that make it worse such as soap, washing detergent, some fabrics or pets, and keep your child cool, since being hot makes eczema itchier [5]. Keep nails short, and use anti-scratch mittens on babies to protect the skin [5].

See a doctor if your child has symptoms of atopic eczema, or if treatments are not helping [4]. Get help urgently if the skin is blistered, crusty, leaking fluid or has pus-filled spots, or if it is painful, swollen or warm, or your child has a high temperature or feels unwell — these can mean infection [4].

text:
Wheezing after running is a common pattern: symptoms often start after physical effort, and in preschool children the main cause of wheezing is viral respiratory infections, according to the SEUP [2][7].

q: my baby has a blocked nose and cant feed properly
text: A blocked nose with a cold is common in babies, and the symptoms usually last 10 to 14 days [3]. To help your baby feed, use saline nose drops from a pharmacy to clear a blocked nose [1], and try smaller feeds more often [1]. The SEUP also suggests nasal washes to keep the nose free of mucus, small frequent feeds to keep feeding and hydration up, and a semi-upright position to make breathing easier [2]. Keep the home free of tobacco smoke and wash your hands often to avoid passing the virus on [2]. If your baby has a high temperature and is uncomfortable, you can give children's paracetamol or children's ibuprofen — always check the leaflet to make sure it is suitable for your child [1].

q: my 2 year old has a temperature of 39.2 and cold hands
text:
A temperature of 39.2°C with cold hands is a fever, and in a 2-year-old a common cold is the usual cause — colds are very frequent in the first years of life, and fever can come with them [6]. Keep offering plenty of fluids, and do nasal washes with saline before feeds and sleep if the nose is blocked [4]. If the fever is over 38°C and your child is uncomfortable, give the anti-fever medicine your doctor normally recommends [4]. Do not use cough syrups, decongestants or mucolytics, especially under 6 years [4]. The fever usually settles within 2 to 3 days, though the cough can last longer [4].

Get urgent medical advice if your child is very tired, irritable or not themselves, is feeding much less than normal, has had a dry nappy for 12 hours or more, or has a temperature of 39°C or higher [2].

q: can I give Nurofen as well
text: No, do not give ibuprofen and paracetamol at the same time, according to the NHS [1]. You can alternate between them only if a doctor or nurse tells you to [1]. If they do, write down when you gave each medicine so the doses are spaced evenly and you do not give too much [1]. Ibuprofen can be given 3 to 4 times in 24 hours, depending on your child's age and dose — check the packet or leaflet [1]. If the paracetamol is not helping your child's symptoms, you can try ibuprofen instead if it is suitable for them [1].

q: my 5 year old complains of stomach ache and won't eat anything
text:
Stomach ache and refusing food can be part of a tummy bug: norovirus causes vomiting, diarrhoea, tummy pain and sometimes a high temperature, and usually gets better in about 2 days, according to the NHS [4]. It can also be a sign of constipation — a stomach ache with bloating or feeling sick, when poos are hard, dry or less often than usual [6].

Offer drinks in small sips often, and let them eat little and often if they want to. Don't force food; if they refuse, take it away calmly and try again later [2]. Two healthy snacks a day between meals is plenty [2].

If your child is active, gaining weight and seems well, they are getting enough to eat, even on days when they eat little [3].

q: my 8 month old hasnt had a wet nappy since this morning
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
No wet nappy since this morning is a sign of dehydration in an infant: no wet diapers for 3 hours or more is one of the symptoms, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Dehydration can be mild, or severe enough to be life-threatening [2].

Offer your baby oral rehydration solution in small amounts, often. The most important thing is to prevent dehydration by giving oral rehydration solutions that come already prepared; do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses from gastroenteritis, according to the SEUP [1]. Keep breastfeeding normally, and even more often if your baby wants it [8]. Do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without checking with your paediatrician [1].

Get medical help right away if there is confusion, fainting, lack of urination, rapid heartbeat or rapid breathing [2].

q: my baby is 4 months and has a fever of 38
text:
A fever is usually the body's normal response to fighting an infection, and most children with a high temperature can be looked after at home [1][2]. It should come down over 1 to 4 days [1].

Keep breastfeeding as normal, and offer plenty of fluids [1]. Check on your baby regularly, including during the night, and keep them at home [1]. Watch for signs of dehydration, such as nappies that are not very wet, sunken eyes, and no tears when crying [1][7]. Do not undress your baby or sponge them down to cool them, and do not cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes [7]. If your baby is distressed or uncomfortable, the NHS says you can give either paracetamol or ibuprofen, checking the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine is suitable, or speaking to a pharmacist or doctor if you are unsure [1]. The dose depends on your child's weight [6].

Get medical advice if you are worried about your baby, or if the medicine is not helping [1].

q: my child got fever after vaccination yesterday
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, fever in the day or two after a vaccination is common and usually settles on its own.

Give plenty of fluids and let them rest. If they are uncomfortable, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen; the dose depends on your child's age and weight, so use the dose your doctor or the leaflet gives, or PediBot's dose calculator for these two medicines.

q: my son fell from bed and vomited twice
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomiting after a head injury
text:
First, do what the warning above says.

A child who vomits after a head injury needs to be checked, and the SEUP lists repeated vomiting among the signs that things may be getting worse after a knock to the head [1]. While you get him seen, keep him resting — no sport, no screens, and quiet physical and mental rest for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the blow was [1]. Offer fluids in small, frequent amounts rather than a large drink all at once [5]. On the way, watch for a headache that is severe or getting worse, confusion or drowsiness, or clear fluid or blood coming from the nose or ears, and tell the staff if you see any of these [1].

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text:
Most insect bites are harmless and usually just itch, and mosquito bites are no exception [5]. The bite should get better in a few days [1].

To ease the itching and swelling, put an ice pack wrapped in a cloth, or a clean cloth soaked in cold water, on the bites for at least 20 minutes, according to the NHS [1]. If the area is swollen, keep it raised where you can [1]. You can use antihistamines to relieve the itching, and a hydrocortisone cream to reduce itching and swelling [1]. Do not let her scratch the bites, as they could get infected, and do not use home remedies like bicarbonate of soda [7].

See a pharmacist if the skin around a bite feels hot, looks red, is painful or swollen, or has pus or fluid coming out, as they can recommend treatments such as antihistamines and steroid creams [7].

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text:
A night-time cough in a 3-year-old is common with several illnesses, and the cough of whooping cough gets worse and happens more often at night [1]. Asthma symptoms also tend to be worse at night and early in the morning [4], and croup is often worse at night too [5].

None of these pages say anything about using a nebulizer, so I can't tell you whether to use one — ask your doctor or pharmacist about that.

What the pages do say: if you think your child may have croup, ask for an urgent appointment — the doctor may give medicine to shorten the illness [5]. See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if asthma treatment is not helping or the symptoms are waking them at night [4]. Whooping cough is treated early with antibiotics, so it's worth having the cough checked [3].

q: my son has been vomiting since morning and cannot keep ORS down
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomits everything and keeps nothing down: it is a danger sign — get seen today
text:
Vomiting that keeps nothing down is a danger sign, and the main risk is dehydration [1][6].

Keep offering oral rehydration solution in small sips, more often than usual, and carry on breastfeeding or formula if your son takes it [7]. Give small sips of extra water too, boiled and cooled first if he is under 6 months [7]. Do not water down formula, and avoid fruit juice and fizzy drinks, which can make vomiting worse [7]. Food is not needed as a fast — small, frequent amounts of his usual diet are fine, avoiding fatty foods, sweets and juices [5].

According to the SEUP, you should go to the emergency department if he vomits a lot and cannot keep down solids or liquids, or vomits even when he takes nothing, or if the vomit is green, contains blood or looks like coffee grounds [4].

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
text:
दस्त आमतौर पर आंतों के संक्रमण का लक्षण है, और यह इलाज योग्य है [3][5]। घर पर सबसे ज़रूरी है ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) — साफ पानी, नमक और चीनी का घोल — पिलाते रहना, जो दस्त में खोए पानी और नमक की भरपाई करता है [1][3]। इसके साथ ज़िंक की खुराक देना भी ज़रूरी है: यह दस्त की अवधि लगभग 25% कम करती है और मल की मात्रा में करीब 30% कमी लाती है [1]। WHO के अनुसार ज़िंक की 10–14 दिन की खुराक दस्त की अवधि घटाती है और नतीजे बेहतर करती है [3]।

खाना न खाने पर घबराएँ नहीं — दस्त के दौरान भी पोषक भोजन, जिसमें माँ का दूध भी शामिल है, देना जारी रखें; इससे कुपोषण और दस्त का चक्र टूटता है [1]।

स्वास्थ्य कर्मी से सलाह लें, खासकर अगर दस्त लंबा चल रहा हो, मल में खून आ रहा हो, या निर्जलीकरण के संकेत दिखें [1]।

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई चीज़ों से हो सकते हैं। खसरा आमतौर पर ज़ुकाम जैसे लक्षणों से शुरू होता है और कुछ दिन बाद दाने निकलते हैं; दाने आमतौर पर चेहरे के बालों की लाइन से शुरू होकर गर्दन, धड़, बाज़ुओं, टांगों और पैरों तक फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है [4]। चेचक में मुख्य लक्षण खुजली वाले दाने हैं, जो शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, और दाने से पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार, दर्द और भूख न लगना भी हो सकता है [5]। हाथ-पैर-मुँह रोग में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, फिर मुँह के छाले और हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे दाने निकलते हैं [3]।

अगर आपको लगे कि बच्चे को खसरा या स्कारलेट फीवर है, तो डॉक्टर से बात करें [1]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में दूध कम पीना और पेशाब कम आना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और जितना छोटा बच्चा हो, निर्जलीकरण का खतरा उतना ही अधिक होता है [1]।

अभी ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, बार-बार देना शुरू करें — घर के बने घोल या कोल्ड ड्रिंक्स न दें [1]। स्तनपान कराने वाली माँ बच्चे की माँग पर सामान्य से भी अधिक बार स्तनपान कराएँ, और फॉर्मूला दूध भी जारी रखें; दूध छोड़ने की ज़रूरत नहीं है [8]। दस्त या उल्टी की दवा बिना बाल रोग विशेषज्ञ से पूछे न दें [1]।

अगर बच्चा बहुत प्यासा लगे, बिना आँसू के रोए, पेशाब कम करे या आँखें धँसी दिखें, या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा, सुस्त या कम प्रतिक्रिया देने लगे, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास जाएँ [1]।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सबसे पहले, ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है वह कीजिए।

सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर ध्यान देना ज़रूरी है। SEUP के मुताबिक़, चोट लगने के बाद 24 से 48 घंटे तक शारीरिक और मानसिक आराम ज़रूरी है — इस दौरान खेल-कूद और मोबाइल, टैबलेट या वीडियो गेम जैसी चीज़ों से दूरी रखें, और बाद में धीरे-धीरे सामान्य गतिविधियों में लौटें [1]।

घर पर इन बातों पर नज़र रखें: तेज़ या बढ़ता हुआ सिरदर्द जो आम दर्द की दवा (पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन) से ठीक न हो, बार-बार उल्टी, भ्रम या बेचैनी, बहुत छोटे बच्चों में चिड़चिड़ापन या जगाने पर मुश्किल से जागना, व्यवहार में बदलाव, चलने या बोलने में दिक्कत, और नाक या कान से खून या साफ़ तरल निकलना [1]।

दवा के बारे में: पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन की खुराक बच्चे के वज़न पर निर्भर करती है — PediBot का डोज़ कैलकुलेटर इन्हीं दोनों के लिए है।

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज़ शिशुओं में रोने के आम कारणों में से एक है, और कुछ शिशुओं में यह कॉलिक के साथ भी जुड़ा होता है [2][5]। अगर बच्चा पॉटी करते समय रोता है, तो उसे आराम देना और शांत करने की कोशिश करना ही सबसे पहला कदम है [1]।

अगर बच्चा लगातार रो रहा है और आप उसे शांत या ध्यान भटका कर चुप नहीं करा पा रहे हैं, या उसका रोना उसके सामान्य रोने जैसा नहीं लगता, तो यह बीमारी का संकेत हो सकता है — ऐसे में अपने डॉक्टर से संपर्क करें [4]। अगर रोने के बीच बच्चा अपनी सामान्य स्थिति में नहीं लौटता, रोने के साथ पीलापन, पसीना, सुस्ती या दूध पीना छोड़ देना हो, या बुखार, उल्टी या खून वाली पॉटी हो, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [6]।

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार के दौरान हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना आम बात है: जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे को ठंड लगती है, कभी-कभी कंपकंपी भी होती है, और खासकर हाथों और पैरों की त्वचा पर जाल जैसा लाल-नीला रंग दिख सकता है, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [2]। जब बुखार उतरता है तो बच्चा पसीना-पसीना हो जाता है, लाल पड़ जाता है और उसे गर्मी लगती है [2]।

बुखार का मतलब है शरीर का तापमान 38°C से ऊपर चला जाना; यह शरीर के अपनी रक्षा करने का तरीका है और अपने आप में गंभीरता की निशानी नहीं है [4]। ज़्यादातर बुखार साधारण, अक्सर वायरल, संक्रमणों से होते हैं [4]।

बुखार में बच्चे को बेचैनी लगती है, भूख कम लगती है, थकान या सिरदर्द हो सकता है [2]। पानी और तरल पदार्थ खूब देना ज़रूरी है ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [1]। अगर बुखार बहुत तेज़ हो, तो डॉक्टर एसिटामिनोफेन या आइबुप्रोफेन जैसी बिना पर्ची की दवा की सलाह दे सकते हैं; बच्चों को एस्पिरिन नहीं देनी चाहिए [1]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न के हिसाब से तय होती है।

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
बच्चे का सुस्त होना और ठीक से जाग न पाना गंभीरता का संकेत है — विकासपीडिया के अनुसार निमोनिया में ये खतरे के लक्षण हैं, और ऐसा लक्षण दिखते ही तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाना चाहिए [2]।

जाते समय बच्चे को गोद में या खटिया पर लिटाकर रखें और साँसों की गति देखते रहें; छह महीने से कम उम्र में 60 से ज़्यादा, छह महीने से दो साल में 50 से ज़्यादा और दो साल से ऊपर 40 से ज़्यादा साँस प्रति मिनट तेज़ श्वसन माना जाता है [3]। बच्चे का खाना-पीना चालू रखने की कोशिश करें [2]।

अस्पताल में बुखार के लिए पैरासिटामोल और श्वास नली खोलने की दवा दी जाती है, और ज़रूरत पड़ने पर ऑक्सीजन या सलाईन भी [2]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न के हिसाब से तय होती है, इसलिए वह डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें [2]।

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
बच्चे का कम पेशाब करना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और SEUP के अनुसार जितना छोटा बच्चा हो, निर्जलीकरण का खतरा उतना ही अधिक होता है [1]।

अभी ओरल रीहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, बार-बार देना सबसे ज़रूरी है — तैयार मिलने वाला पैकेट ही इस्तेमाल करें, घर के बने घोल या कोल्ड ड्रिंक न दें [1]। अगर बच्चा बहुत प्यासा लगे, बिना आँसू के रोए, कम पेशाब करे या आँखें धँसी दिखें, तो यह चिंता की बात है [1]। दस्त या उल्टी की दवा बिना डॉक्टर से पूछे न दें [1]।

खाना बंद करने की ज़रूरत नहीं; सामान्य खाना थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, ज़्यादा बार दें, और स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, माँगने पर और भी अधिक कराएँ [8]। चिकनी चीज़ें, मिठाई और जूस से बचें; स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक भी न दें [8]।

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
सबसे पहले, ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है वह कीजिए।

अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है [2]।

बुखार शरीर का संक्रमण से लड़ने का स्वाभाविक तरीका है [2]। त्वचा पर ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर भी न मिटें, बुखार के साथ गंभीर संकेत हैं [1][2]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें, और उसे ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े उतारकर स्पंज न करें [2]। 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। 2 महीने से छोटे बच्चे को पैरासिटामोल न दें, और 3 महीने से छोटे, 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले, चिकनपॉक्स या निर्जलीकरण वाले बच्चे को इबुप्रोफेन न दें [2]। डॉक्टर के कहे बिना इबुप्रोफेन और पैरासिटामोल बारी-बारी न दें [2]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर है, इसलिए वह डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें [2]।

बुखार आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में सामान्य हो जाता है [3]।

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text:
Aapke 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar hai, to paracetamol dene se pehle uske vazan ke hisaab se dose tay hoti hai — dawa ki matra bachche ke vazan par nirbhar karti hai [3]. Paracetamol har 4 se 6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, aur din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi [3]. Isse zyada dene par liver ko nuksan ho sakta hai [3].

Bukhar ke saath bechaini ya takleef ho to paracetamol diya ja sakta hai [1]. Agar bachcha so raha hai to use jagakar dawa dene ki zarurat nahi [6]. Dawa ke saath-saath kapde kam karein, taral padarth dein aur halki activity rakhein [6].

Agar aapne packet ya leaflet par likhe se zyada paracetamol de diya hai, to turant medical salah lein [7].

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi hona bachchon mein aam hai, aur yeh asthma ka bhi ek lakshan ho sakta hai [1]. Agar bachche ko saans lene mein takleef, tez saans, ya seene mein kasav ho, to yeh asthma ke lakshan hain [1]. SEUP ke mutabik, khansi ke saath saans phoolna, seene ka dhasna, pasliyan dikhna aur saans chhodte waqt seeti ki awaaz (sibilancias) bhi ho sakti hai [3].

Ghar par: kamre mein saaf humidifier ya thanda vaporizer lagaayein, aur bachche ko khoob taral (paani, doodh) dein [6]. Kisi bhi khansi ya sardi ki dawa dene se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochhein, kyunki kuch dawaiyan bachchon ke liye theek nahi hoti [6]. Aspirin bilkul na dein [6].

Agar saans lene mein sakht takleef, hothon ya chehre par neela rang, ya khansi lagatar badhti ho, to turant medical madad lein [1][3].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Aapke bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli heat rash (prickly heat) ho sakti hai — yeh uncomfortable hoti hai par aam taur par harmless hai aur kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jati hai [6]. Iske symptoms hain chhote ubhre hue dane, khujli ya chubhan wali feeling, aur halki sujan [6].

Abhi yeh karein: skin ko thanda rakhein taaki pasina na aaye aur rash na bade — dheele cotton kapde pehnayein, halki rajai use karein, thande paani se nahayein, aur dehydration se bachne ke liye khoob paani pilayein [6]. Khujli ya chubhan shant karne ke liye thandi cheez (geela kapda ya tea towel mein lipti ice pack) 20 minute tak lagayein, aur rash ko kharochne ke bajaye thap-thap karein [6]. Perfumed shower gel ya cream use na karein [6].

Agar aap sure nahi hain ki yeh heat rash hai, to doosre rashes ko dekhein [6].
sources: [6] NHS — "Heat rash (prickly heat)" (2024), section "Heat rash (prickly heat)", p. 1 — ht

q: mera bachcha bed se gir gaya aur ek baar ulti ki
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सबसे पहले, ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है वह कीजिए।

Girne ke baad ek baar ulti hona SEUP ke mutabik aise mamle mein dekha jane wala lakshan hai [1]. Ghar par sharirik aur mansik aaram 24 se 48 ghante tak rakhein, jitna gol chot gehra tha utna zyada; is dauran khel-kood aur mobile, tablet ya video game bilkul na dein [1]. Uske baad hi dhire-dhire normal kaam par wapas laayein [1].

Dhyan rakhein: tez ya badhta sar dard jo aam dawa se theek na ho, baar-baar ulti, bhram ya confusion, chhote bachchon mein chidchidapan ya jagaana mushkil, vyavhaar mein badlav, chalne ya bolne mein dikkat, aur naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani aana [1].
sources: [1] SEUP — "Traumatismo craneal. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO PUEDE V

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Kabz mein potty karte waqt bachche ka dard aur rona aam baat hai, aur yeh colic jaisa bhi ho sakta hai — SEUP ke mutabik colic ke kai kaaranon mein se ek kaaran kabz bhi hai [2].

Jo aap abhi kar sakte hain: bachche ko aaram se pakde rakhein aur tasalli dein; NHS kehta hai ki kabhi kabhi tasalli ke alawa kuch zyada nahi kiya ja sakta, aur rona dheere-dheere khud shaant ho jata hai [1]. Agar rona khaane ke waqt hota hai, to breastfeeding mein positioning aur attachment sudharna madad karta hai [5].

Colic aksar 5 mahine se chhote bachchon mein hota hai [1], aur SEUP ke mutabik yeh 15 din ki umar se shuru hokar 5-6 hafte mein apne shikhar par hota hai aur 4 mahine ke baad kam hi rehta hai [6].

Agar bachcha lagatar ro raha hai aur aap use shaant ya distract nahi kar pa rahe, ya rona uske normal rone jaisa nahi lag raha, to yeh bimaari ka sanket ho sakta hai — apne doctor se milein [7].

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: साँस लेने में गंभीर दिक्कत (पसलियाँ दिखना, बहुत तेज़ साँस, साँस रुकना, नीलापन)
text:
सबसे पहले, ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है वह कीजिए।

Saans lene mein dikkat kai cheezon se ho sakti hai, jaise RSV, bronchiolitis ya croup, aur inme shuruaat mein nazla-khansi jaisi halki nishaniyan hoti hain [2][4][5]. Croup mein khansi kutton jaisi lagti hai, awaaz baith jaati hai aur saans lete waqt tez, kadwi awaaz aati hai [3].

Jo ab karna hai: bachche ko seedha aur aaram se rakhein, khana-peena thoda-thoda par baar-baar dein, aur saans lene mein madad ke liye unhe shaant rakhein [4][5]. Agar bachcha doodh ya khana theek se nahi le raha, to use chhote-chhote ghoont ya chammach se baar-baar dein [5].

Turant madad lein agar bachche ki saans bahut tez ho, pasliyan andar khinch rahi hon, saans mein rukawat aaye, ya honth, jeebh ya skin neeli ya grey ho jaye [1][5].

q: meri beti bahut sust hai aur jag nahi rahi
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
Bahut sust hona aur jag nahi paana ek aisi sthiti hai jismein turant madad leni chahiye — SEUP kehta hai ki excessive drowsiness ya sust hona ek warning sign hai jiske liye aapko emergency department jaana chahiye [1].

Jab tak aap madad ke liye ja rahe hain, apni beti ko apne paas rakhein, use hilaayein aur dekhein ki woh aapki awaaz ya touch par koi response deti hai ya nahi [1]. Agar woh bilkul bhi response na de, to ise turant batayein [1].

Agar saath mein saans lene mein dikkat ho — pasliyaan saaf dikhein, bahut tez saans le, ya saans mein pause ho — to yeh bhi ek emergency sign hai [1].

q: mera bachcha bahut tez saans le raha hai
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
तेज़ साँस लेना शिशुओं में RSV (रेस्पिरेटरी सिंसिशियल वायरस) का लक्षण हो सकता है, जो शुरू में हल्का रहता है पर कुछ दिनों में गंभीर हो सकता है [2]। शिशुओं में इसके लक्षणों में नाक बहना, कम खाना-पीना, खाँसी और साँस लेने में कठिनाई या घरघराहट शामिल हैं [2][4]।

अभी बच्चे को थोड़ा-थोड़ा और बार-बार दूध या तरल देना जारी रखें, ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [3]। बच्चे को सीधा या थोड़ा ऊपर उठाकर रखें और आराम दें।

WHO के अनुसार, 5 साल से छोटे बच्चों में खाँसी या साँस लेने में कठिनाई के साथ तेज़ साँस चलना (टैकीपनिया) या पसलियों के नीचे धँसाव निमोनिया का संकेत हो सकता है, इसलिए ऐसे बच्चे को जाँच करानी चाहिए [6]। बहुत गंभीर रूप से प्रभावित शिशु दूध या पानी नहीं ले पाते और बेहोश हो सकते हैं [6]।

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common with whooping cough, an infection of the lungs and breathing tubes that spreads easily and can be serious [3]. The coughing bouts can last for a few minutes, are worse at night, and may end with a "whoop" sound or vomiting [3]. Fits of rapid coughs followed by a high-pitched whoop, vomiting during or after coughing, and exhaustion after the fits are typical, and these fits get worse and more frequent, especially at night [4].

Keep the room cool and the bedding light, since sweating at night is normal when the room or bedding is too hot [2]. Ask a pharmacist about cough medicine, but some cough medicines should not be given to children under 12 years old [1].

Ask for an urgent appointment or get help from your local emergency number if your child has a very bad cough that is getting worse [5]. Get emergency help if their lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey, or if they are finding it hard to breathe properly [5].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash of small, raised bumps that feels rough, like sandpaper, could be scarlet fever, according to the NHS [5]. A spotty rash that starts on the head or neck and spreads to the rest of the body could be measles [5]. Measles usually starts with cold-like symptoms — a high temperature, runny or blocked nose, sneezing, cough, and red, sore, watery eyes — followed by a rash a few days later [5]. The measles rash begins as flat red spots at the hairline and spreads down to the neck, trunk, arms, legs and feet, and small raised bumps may appear on top [4].

Speak to a GP if you think your child has scarlet fever or measles [5].

q: should I give polio drops if my baby already had injection
text: The polio vaccine is given both as an injection and as drops, and they are not interchangeable — the injection (IPV) and the drops (OPV) protect in different ways, so a child who has had the injection may still be offered drops [4]. Whether your baby needs the drops now depends on the schedule they are following and what they have already received [2]. If a dose was missed, contact your doctor, who will advise what vaccination your child should get and when [1][3]. Tell the doctor or nurse about any illnesses or allergies your baby has had before vaccination [5].

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text: It's natural to worry when a child refuses to eat, but it's more helpful to think about what they eat over a week than in a single day, according to the NHS [5]. If your child is active, gaining weight and seems well, they're getting enough to eat [5]. Keep offering a variety of foods from the 4 main food groups — fruit and vegetables; potatoes, bread, rice, pasta and other starchy carbohydrates; dairy or dairy alternatives; and beans, pulses, fish, eggs, meat and other proteins — and keep going back to foods they refused before, as children's tastes change [5]. Give small portions, praise them for eating even a little, and don't force or leave meals until they're too hungry or tired [3]. Get medical help if your child is unwell and getting worse, or is eating much less than normal [6].

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A congested chest with a whistling noise in a 6-month-old can be bronchiolitis, which often starts like a cold and then brings a cough, faster breathing and noisy breathing (wheezing), according to the NHS [2]. Symptoms are usually worst between days 3 and 5, and the cough usually gets better in 3 weeks [2].

Keep feeding your baby as normally as you can, and offer feeds more often in smaller amounts if they are finding it hard to feed [2]. Watch their nappies: a dry nappy for 12 hours or more, or other signs of dehydration, needs medical help [2].

Get help today if your baby is feeding much less than normal, has had a dry nappy for 12 hours or more, or seems very tired or irritable [2]. Trust your own judgement if you feel your child is seriously unwell [2].

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में तेज़ बुखार बहुत आम है और तापमान आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में सामान्य हो जाता है [1]। बुखार का मतलब 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान है [1]।

घर पर ही देखभाल की जा सकती है: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान करता है तो सामान्य रूप से स्तनपान जारी रखें, निर्जलीकरण के संकेतों पर नज़र रखें, भूख लगे तो खाना दें, और रात में भी नियमित रूप से बच्चे को देखते रहें [4]। अगर बच्चा परेशान या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दी जा सकती है — पैकेजिंग या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा बच्चे के लिए उपयुक्त है [4]। 3 महीने से कम उम्र के बच्चे को, या जिसका वज़न 5 किलो से कम हो, आइबुप्रोफेन न दें [2]।

अगर बच्चा 3 से 6 महीने का है और तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा है, या बुखार के साथ दाने जैसे बीमारी के और संकेत हैं, तो डॉक्टर से सलाह लें [2]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाना या स्पंज करना नहीं चाहिए — तेज़ तापमान शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, इसलिए बच्चे के कपड़े न उतारें और न ही उसे ठंडा करने के लिए पानी से पोंछें [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में अपने आप सामान्य हो जाता है [1]। तापमान डिजिटल थर्मामीटर से बगल में नापें [1]। अगर बच्चे ने अभी नहाया है या कंबल में लपेटा गया है, तो तापमान कुछ देर के लिए ज़्यादा दिख सकता है — कुछ मिनट रुककर फिर नापें [1]।

6 महीने के बच्चे को 2 महीने से कम उम्र में पैरासिटामोल न दें, और 3 महीने से कम उम्र या 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले बच्चे को इबुप्रोफेन न दें [7]। बुखार की दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न के अनुसार तय होती है — अपने डॉक्टर से पूछें।

अगर बच्चा 3 से 6 महीने का है और तापमान 39C या ज़्यादा है, या उसे दौरा पड़ा हो, गर्दन अकड़ गई हो, त्वचा का रंग बदल गया हो, या वह सुस्त और जगाने पर मुश्किल से जागे, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [7]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

[7] NHS — "High temperature (fever) in children" (2025), section "Don’t", p. 1 — https://w

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
सूखी खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ ब्रोंकियल (श्वसन मार्ग) में रुकावट से होती है, जिससे खांसी, सांस लेने में तकलीफ़ और सीने में सीटी की आवाज़ आती है, और यह ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवाओं जैसे सालबुटामोल देने पर ठीक हो जाती है, SEUP के अनुसार [2]। प्रीस्कूल उम्र के बच्चों में सीटी की आवाज़ का मुख्य कारण सांस की वायरल संक्रमण होता है [2]।

अभी बच्चे को आराम से बैठाकर रखें और शांत रखें, और सांस लेने में मदद के लिए जिस दवा (इनहेलर/ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर) की सलाह डॉक्टर ने दी हो, उसे बताए अनुसार दें; दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न के अनुसार तय होती है [2]।

अगर बच्चे की हालत बिगड़ रही हो या डॉक्टर से मिलने के बाद भी सुधार न हो, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें, NHS के अनुसार [3]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल दाने और खुजली कई वजहों से हो सकते हैं। बहुत खुजली वाले उभरे दाने छोटे माइट्स (स्केबीज़) से भी हो सकते हैं, जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देते हैं और तेज़ खुजली व दाने करते हैं, और आमतौर पर इसे घर पर ही इलाज किया जा सकता है [4]। स्केबीज़ त्वचा के सीधे संपर्क से फैलता है, और यह सफ़ाई की कमी से नहीं होता [1]।

अगर दाने गर्मी से हुए हैं, तो त्वचा को ठंडा रखें: ढीले सूती कपड़े पहनाएँ, हल्का बिस्तर इस्तेमाल करें, ठंडे पानी से नहलाएँ, और पानी खूब पिलाएँ [6]। खुजली शांत करने के लिए ठंडी चीज़ (गीला कपड़ा या तौलिये में लपेटी आइस पैक) 20 मिनट तक लगाएँ, और खुजाने की जगह थपथपाएँ; सुगंधित साबुन या क्रीम न लगाएँ [6]।

अगर बच्चा 2 साल से छोटा हो और स्केबीज़ के लक्षण हों, घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ हो, त्वचा में संक्रमण या एक्ज़िमा जैसी दूसरी त्वचा समस्या हो, या फ़ार्मेसी का इलाज करने के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे, तो डॉक्टर को दिखाएँ [1]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text: एमएमआर वैक्सीन के बारे में सीधे तौर पर सुरक्षा की बात करने वाली जानकारी स्रोतों में नहीं है। स्रोतों में यह बताया गया है कि लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के थोड़े-बहुत दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, जो मामूली से लेकर गंभीर तक हो सकते हैं, फिर भी ये सारे टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं [6]। दुष्प्रभावों का इलाज मामूली उपचार से हो सकता है [6]। भारत के राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम में इस्तेमाल होने वाली वैक्सीन्स के मुख्य दुष्प्रभावों और उनके उपचार का विवरण स्रोत में दिया गया है [6]। टीकाकरण का समय और कौन-सा टीका कब लगेगा, यह भारत के राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होता है।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Aapke 8 mahine ke baby ko sir ka chot laga hai — SEUP ke mutabik ye aam taur par girne se hota hai [1]. Abhi shaant rahein aur baby ko aaram dein: 24 se 48 ghante tak sharirik aur mansik aaram zaroori hai, koi khel ya screen nahi [2]. Baby so sakta hai, lekin zyada bade chot mein use har 4 ghante jagana chahiye [6]. Khana-peena pehle jaisa hi chalega, koi khaas diet nahi chahiye [6].

In lakshanon par nazar rakhein: tez ya badhta sir dard jo dawa se theek na ho, baar-baar ulti, confusion ya bechaini, aur bahut chhote bachhon mein chidchidapan ya jagane mein mushkil [2]. Naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani aana bhi chinta ki baat hai [2].

Turant doctor ke paas jaayein agar ulti ya dard badhe, convulsion ho, behoshi ya kamzori dikhe, ya baby ko jagana mushkil ho [4]. Agar girne ki unchai 1 meter se zyada thi to bhi turant dikhayein [5].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche mein badan par laal daane kai alag-alag bimariyon mein ho sakte hain, aur inmein se koi bhi akele daane dekhkar batana mushkil hai. WHO ke mutabik khaaj (scabies) mein tez khujli hoti hai, khaas taur par raat mein, aur ungliyon, kalaiyon, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas daane aur lakeerein dikhti hain [1]. Khaaj chhote bachchon mein zyada gambhir daane deti hai, khaas taur par hatheli, talwe aur sar ki twacha par [1].

MedlinePlus ke mutabik chhechak (varicella) mein khujli wale daane pehle chehre, chhaati aur peeth par aate hain, phir poore sharir par phailte hain, aur ye paani wale chhaale ban kar phir paapdi jamate hain [4]. WHO ke mutabik khasra (measles) mein tez bukhar, khansi, naak behna aur aankhein laal hone ke 3 se 5 din baad daane aate hain, jo chehre se shuru hokar neeche ki taraf phailte hain [3].

Daane ke saath tez bukhar, khansi, naak behna ya aankhein laal hon to turant doctor se milna chahiye [3].

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text: Diarrhoea after a trip is usually an infection picked up from contaminated food or water, and it is treated with oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools, according to the WHO [1]. Give ORS in small amounts often, and keep offering nutrient-rich foods and breast milk during the episode [1]. Zinc supplements are also part of treatment: they shorten the episode by about 25% and reduce stool volume by around 30% [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or soft drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3]. See a health professional if the diarrhoea is persistent, if there is blood in the stool, or if there are signs of dehydration [1].

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Dizziness after being in the sun can be a sign of heat exhaustion, according to the NHS [4]. Heat exhaustion usually does not need emergency help if the person can cool down within 30 minutes [4].

Cool them down and give them fluids [4]. Move them out of the heat, into the shade or indoors, and have them drink cold drinks [2][4]. Loosen or remove extra clothing and let them rest.

Get medical help right away if they become confused or restless, have a very high temperature with hot skin that is not sweating, breathe fast, have a seizure, or lose consciousness — these are signs of heatstroke, which is a medical emergency [5].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text:
Loose, watery stools are common in children and usually get better on their own within a day or two [4]. The main treatment is to replace the fluids and salts your child is losing, according to MedlinePlus [1].

Give your child an oral rehydration solution, which you can buy without a prescription, in small sips often [1][3]. The WHO says diarrhoea should be treated with oral rehydration solution — a mix of clean water, sugar and salt — and that a 10–14 day course of zinc tablets shortens how long it lasts [2]. Keep offering it as long as the loose stools continue.

Contact your doctor right away if your child has a change in mental state such as irritability or lack of energy, diarrhoea lasting more than a day, any fever in an infant, frequent loose stools, vomiting often, severe belly pain, or signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet nappies for 3 hours or more, and no tears when crying [6].

q: is MMR vaccine safe for my daughter
text: Yes, the MMR vaccine is safe. Like all medicines it can cause side effects, but not everyone gets them, and the common ones are usually mild and last only 2 to 3 days, according to the NHS [4]. These can include a raised, blotchy rash, feeling unwell and a high temperature around 7 to 11 days after the vaccination, or swollen glands around the cheeks, neck and jaw and aching joints around 2 to 3 weeks after it [4]. More serious side effects, such as a severe allergic reaction, are rare, and the person who vaccinates your child is trained to treat them immediately [4]. The MMR vaccine is not linked to autism: research has shown there is no link [4]. Protection starts within 2 weeks of the vaccine, and after 2 doses around 99% of people are protected against measles and rubella and around 88% against mumps [1]. In India, the ages for each dose follow the national schedule.

q: my 6 month old has started solids, can I give banana
text: Banana is a good first food to offer at around 6 months, when your baby is starting solids [4]. At the beginning, how much they eat matters less than getting used to the idea of eating — they still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [4]. You can offer it mashed or as a soft finger food and let them feed themselves; there is no more risk of choking when a baby feeds themselves than when fed with a spoon [1]. Keep breastfeeding or giving first infant formula until at least 1 year, and offer sips of water with meals from around 6 months [3][5]. If your baby was born prematurely, ask your health visitor or GP when to start solids [4].

q: my 5 year old has stomach pain and constipation
text:
Stomach ache is a common symptom in children and most causes are harmless and get better on their own, such as constipation, gas or a tummy bug, according to the SEUP [2]. Constipation often comes with a stomach ache and feeling bloated or sick [1].

For the constipation, the main thing is to give more fluids, preferably water, and more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables. Don't replace fruit with juice, as juice has little fibre [3]. Keep to a regular routine and don't let them hold in the urge to go to the toilet [3]. Most cases of constipation in children are not caused by any illness, and it's not essential for a child to poo every day [3]. Don't give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [3].

See a doctor if the pain is severe, if they seem very unwell and complain a lot, if there is blood in the poo, or if they vomit many times and can't keep down food or drink [3].

q: my 3 year old has malaria fever or maybe teething, how can I tell
text:
Malaria and teething are not told apart by the fever alone: the first symptoms of malaria may be mild and similar to many other illnesses, and hard to recognise as malaria, according to the WHO [1]. The most common early symptoms are fever, headache and chills [1]. In young children, malaria can become severe quickly — left untreated, it can progress to severe illness within 24 hours [1]. Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1].

Because of that, a fever in a 3-year-old who may have been in a malaria area is not something to sort out at home. Malaria is preventable and curable, and treatment can stop mild cases from getting worse [1]. If you are in or have travelled to an area where malaria is common, your child needs to be seen and tested by a doctor, who will decide on treatment [1][2].

q: my child has been scratching small bumps on his body
text:
An itchy rash of raised bumps or patches in many shapes and sizes is the main symptom of hives, according to the NHS [3]. Hives rashes usually get better within a few days, and you can often treat them yourself [5].

Try not to let him scratch — scratching a bite or sting can let it get infected [6]. If the skin around a bite feels hot, looks red, is painful, looks swollen, or has pus or fluid coming out, see a pharmacist: they can recommend antihistamines and steroid creams, and give the same antibiotics as a doctor if it is infected [6]. For a child under 1 year old with an insect bite or sting, see a doctor [6].

Get urgent help if symptoms get worse or are not getting better, if he has tummy pain and is being sick, feels dizzy or lightheaded, or has a high temperature with swollen glands [6].

q: my daughter has fever after coming back from a trip
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, a high temperature is very common and usually settles within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [1]. A fever is not an illness in itself — it is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most fevers are caused by infections, MedlinePlus says [3].

Check the temperature with a digital thermometer in the armpit, and if they have just had a bath or been wrapped up, wait a few minutes and try again [1]. Keep them drinking enough fluids to prevent dehydration [3]. Do not undress or sponge them down, do not cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes, and do not give aspirin to a child under 16 [7]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen may be recommended if the fever is very high, but never ibuprofen for a child under 3 months, under 5kg, with chickenpox, dehydrated, or with asthma unless a doctor advises it [3][7].

Because they were travelling, contact your doctor when you return home if they were feverish while away [6]. See a doctor if the fever lasts 5 days or more, or if they are not eating or not themselves [7].

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time
text: Start with single vegetables and fruits, mashed or as soft cooked sticks — parsnip, broccoli, potato, yam, sweet potato, carrot, apple or pear [5]. Include less sweet ones like broccoli, cauliflower and spinach so your baby gets used to a range of flavours [5]. Let any cooked food cool right down first [5]. At first, how much they eat matters less than getting used to eating; they still get most energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [2]. Introduce foods containing allergens — peanuts, hens' eggs, gluten, fish — one at a time and in small amounts, from around 6 months [5]. Cows' milk can be used in cooking or mixed with food, but not as a main drink until 1 year [5]. Babies do not need salt or sugar added to their food or cooking water [5]. If your baby was born prematurely, ask your health visitor or GP when to start solids [2].

q: my 4 year old has severe cough and catarrh
text: A severe cough with catarrh (a runny nose) can be the first phase of whooping cough, which usually lasts 1 to 2 weeks and looks like a cold, with fever, runny nose, red watery eyes, and a mild or occasional cough and sneezing, according to the Government of Canada [4]. In the second phase, which lasts 1 to 6 weeks, the cough becomes more severe, with uncontrollable coughing fits that can make it hard to breathe and may cause vomiting after the fits [4]. For older children who have been vaccinated, the symptoms may be less severe [4]. Treatment depends on your child's age and how long they have had the infection; if whooping cough is diagnosed within 3 weeks of the cough starting, antibiotics are given to help stop it spreading to others, though they may not reduce symptoms, and the full course must be completed, according to the NHS [6]. Hospital treatment is usually needed for severe whooping cough [6].

A high temperature is very common in young children, and it usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days [1]. A temperature of 38C or more counts as a fever [1].

Keep giving plenty of fluids — if your baby is breastfed, continue to breastfeed as normal. Offer food if they want it, check on them regularly including during the night, and keep them at home. q: my 5 year old fell down and hurt his leg leg is swollen
text:
A swollen leg after a fall is usually treated with PRICE therapy for the first 2 to 3 days, according to the NHS: protect the injury, rest it and try not to put weight on it, apply an ice pack (or a bag of frozen vegetables wrapped in a tea towel) for up to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours, wrap a bandage around it during the day, and keep it raised on a pillow as much as possible [2]. Avoid heat, alcohol and massages for the first couple of days, and once he can move the leg without pain stopping him, keep it moving so it does not get stiff [2].

If the leg is very painful, badly swollen or he cannot put any weight on it, have him seen by a doctor.

q: my 18 month old is refusing food and crying when chewing
text:
It is common for toddlers to refuse food sometimes, and it is normal for them to refuse to eat or even taste new foods, according to the NHS [3]. What matters is what they eat over a week, not in a day: if your child is active, gaining weight and seems well, they are getting enough [3]. A high temperature is very common in young children and is usually the body's natural response to fighting an infection like a cough or cold [1][3]. Shivering is part of how the body raises its temperature, and it is not a sign of harm by itself [6].

Fever usually settles within 1 to 4 days [1]. Get urgent help if your child has a stiff neck, a rash that does not fade when you press a glass against it, is bothered by light, has a fit, has unusually cold hands and feet, is drowsy and hard to wake, is confused, or has difficulty breathing [3].

banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
First, do what the warning above says.

A child who is not drinking and has very little urine is losing more fluid than they are taking in, and that is what causes dehydration [2]. Offer small sips of water or ice chips if they are having trouble keeping liquids down [4]. Oral rehydration solutions are made for children and you can buy them without a prescription; they replace the fluids and electrolytes lost [5]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace losses from gastroenteritis, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [1]. Keep offering fluids regularly, and food with a high water content such as soup, jelly or melon [6].

text: A blocked nose can make breastfeeding harder, and breastfeeding is still worth continuing: breast milk protects babies from common infections and gives them the right balance of nutrients [3]. If you are having trouble with breastfeeding, contact a breastfeeding specialist [3]. Mothers and families should get support to breastfeed, and babies should feed as often as they ask, day and night [2]. If you are worried about whether you should breastfeed, talk to your doctor [3].

q: my 3 year old has severe chest congestion and flu
text:
Chest congestion and flu in a 3-year-old is usually a viral illness that gets better within a few days, according to the NHS [2]. Flu can cause a blocked nose, cough, tiredness and a high temperature [2].

There is no medicine that cures flu: antibiotics do not work for viral infections such as flu, and doctors do not recommend them because they will not relieve symptoms or speed recovery [5]. Keep offering fluids and small, frequent feeds, and let your child rest.

Get medical help if your child is not waking up or interacting, has difficulty breathing, is not drinking or eating as usual, or is not wanting to play or be held, according to the Government of Canada [1]. Also seek help if your child is unwell and getting worse, is feeding or eating much less than normal, has a dry nappy for 12 hours or more, or is very tired or irritable [2].

q: what solids to give first to 6 month baby
text: At around 6 months, start with a variety of foods alongside breast milk or first infant formula — how much they eat matters less than getting used to eating [3]. You can offer purées, mashed or soft finger foods, or a mix; there is no right or wrong way, and self-feeding carries no more choking risk than spoon-feeding [1]. Continue breast milk or first infant formula until at least 1 year, and offer sips of water from an open or free-flow cup with meals [4][5]. Sit your baby upright in a high chair with a safety harness, and never leave them unattended on a raised surface [5]. If your baby was born prematurely, ask your health visitor or GP when to start solids [3].
